title: Design Handoff & Developer Specs
description: Bridge the gap between design and development by writing precise design specifications. Tests design system mapping, redlining, and CSS layout coordination.

seo.overviewBody: Design handoff bridges the gap between design vision and technical production code. Senior UI designers prove readiness by organizing Figma files, producing detailed redline annotations, exporting clean assets (SVG/WebP), mapping design tokens, and performing design QA reviews.

deliverables.title: 1. Comprehensive Design Handoff Document & Specs
deliverables.desc: Developer-ready Figma handoff file featuring redline spatial measurements, responsive behavior notes, and component token mappings.

deliverables.title: 2. Asset Export & Developer Token Library
deliverables.desc: Clean export package of optimized SVG icons, WebP imagery, and JSON design token definitions.

deliverables.title: 3. Design QA Audit Checklist
deliverables.desc: Design QA checklist for reviewing staging builds against original Figma design specifications.

faqs.question: How should Figma files be organized for seamless developer handoff?
faqs.answer: Separate files into Cover, User Flows, Dev-Ready Screens, and Archive pages. Clearly label component states, auto-layout properties, and token variables.

faqs.question: What are redline annotations in design handoffs?
faqs.answer: Redline annotations explicitly document padding, margin spacing, font sizes, line heights, component states, and responsive breakpoint rules for developers.

faqs.question: What is Design QA?
faqs.answer: Design QA is the process where designers inspect front-end staging builds to verify that visual styling, layout spacing, fonts, and micro-interactions accurately match original design specs before release.
